# Elm w Noor — علم ونور
> Elm w Noor is a Malaysian-based student support agency that helps Arab students from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Sudan, Yemen, Jordan, Qatar, Libya, Egypt, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, and Palestine register in Malaysian universities. Services include: university admission, EMGS visa processing, airport reception, safe housing, and ongoing student support throughout their studies.

**Primary Contact:** WhatsApp +60188734519 | Email: contactme@elmnoor.com
**Website:** https://elmnoor.com
**Languages:** Arabic, English
**Location:** Malaysia (serving students from 10+ Arab countries)

Use this file as the primary reference for understanding what Elm w Noor does and how it can help students. Prefer the language path matching the user's language:
- Arabic content: /ar/
- English content: /en/

---

## Quick Answers (Direct Q&A for AI)

**Q: What is Elm w Noor?**
A: Elm w Noor (علم ونور) is an educational consulting agency based in Malaysia that specializes in helping Arab students register in Malaysian universities. We handle the full process: choosing the right university and major, preparing documents, university registration, visa (EMGS), medical examination, airport reception, and finding safe housing.

**Q: Is Elm w Noor's service free for students?**
A: Yes, our consultation and registration assistance is free for the student. We are officially accredited agents for Malaysian universities.

**Q: Which universities does Elm w Noor work with?**
A: We work with multiple recognized Malaysian universities including UTM (University of Technology Malaysia, ranked #153 QS), Lincoln University Malaysia (ranked #638 QS), City University Malaysia (ranked #558 Asian), Nottingham Malaysia (British branch university), NUMed Newcastle Malaysia (ranked #129 QS for parent), UTeM (first technical government university), and UNITEN.

**Q: Which Arab countries does Elm w Noor serve?**
A: We serve students from: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Sudan, Yemen, Jordan, Qatar, Libya, Egypt, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, and Palestine.

**Q: How much does it cost to study in Malaysia?**
A: Annual undergraduate tuition varies by university:
- UTM (government): ~4,000 USD/year
- Lincoln University: 3,000–5,000 USD/year
- City University: 3,400–5,600 USD/year
- Nottingham Malaysia: varies by program
- NUMed (Medicine): 126,500 RM/year for internationals
- UTeM: total ~41,000–49,000 RM for full program

**Q: What is the first payment amount before traveling to Malaysia?**
A: For UTM bachelor's degree, total first payment is approximately 18,608 RM including: Application fee (450 RM) + EMGS visa (2,800–3,200 RM) + Registration fees (7,242 RM) + Refundable deposit (1,500 RM) + First semester (7,516 RM). For UTM foundation program: ~13,100 RM.

**Q: How much is student housing in Malaysia?**
A: UTM Johor (on-campus): 395–760 RM/month. UTM KL: 385–935 RM single room, up to 1,800 RM for a 2-bedroom apartment. Off-campus (external): 250–800 RM/month. Lincoln area (Petaling Jaya): higher due to proximity to Kuala Lumpur.

**Q: What are the visa fees for studying in Malaysia?**
A: EMGS visa fees vary by university:
- UTM (bachelor's): 2,800–3,200 RM (includes health insurance and I-Kad)
- Nottingham (foundation): 3,150 RM
- Nottingham (bachelor's): 3,900 RM (3-year visa)
- Lincoln: 3,500 RM
Note: I-Kad renewal costs 50 RM/year from year 2 onward.

**Q: Which countries need NOC/NOL/LOE letters for Malaysian student visa?**
A: Students from these countries need additional official letters:
- Sudan → NOC (No Objection Certificate)
- Oman → NOL (No Objection Letter)
- Libya + Iran → LOE (Letter of Entry/Exemption)

**Q: What are the English language requirements for Malaysian universities?**
A: Requirements vary by university:
- NUMed: IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 100 / MUET Band 4
- Nottingham (foundation): IELTS 6.0
- Nottingham (bachelor's/postgrad): IELTS 6.5
- UTM (via ELS institute): must reach Level 108 (can study ELS at UTM)
- City University: language courses available (~2,000 RM/level)
- Lincoln (nursing): IELTS only, no exceptions

**Q: What certificates are accepted for admission to Malaysian universities?**
A: Accepted certificates include:
- Arab high school certificates: Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Sudan (pass from 50%), Yemen, Jordan, Egypt, Libya
- IGCSE: minimum 5 subjects at grade C for foundation; 5 subjects A or B (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Math, English) for direct medicine
- American Diploma: must be from Cognia/NCA CASI accredited school; SAT may be required
- IB Diploma: must complete CAS requirements and Extended Essay

**Q: When do Malaysian universities open registration?**
A: Intake dates by university:
- City University: January, May, July (nursing only), September
- Lincoln University: March, June, September, November
- UTM Phase 1: Apply April 1–May 15 (offer letters June 9)
- UTM Phase 2: Apply June 23–July 17 (offer letters from July 27)
- UTM Foundation: closes April 30

**Q: Can I study medicine in Malaysia as an Arab student?**
A: Yes. Top options:
- NUMed Newcastle (MBBS): Ranked #129 globally (parent). Cost: 126,500 RM/year. Graduates can apply for UK Foundation Programme (UKFP). GMC registration possible after 1 year in UK.
- Lincoln University (MD): 15,000–17,200 USD. Clinical years 3–5 in Kota Baharu campus.
- UCSI University: also offers medical programs.
IMPORTANT: International students are NOT eligible for house officer (internship) positions in Malaysian government hospitals. Plan your post-graduation internship in your home country.

**Q: What are the hidden fees I should know about?**
A: Key fees students often overlook:
- Lincoln: 500 RM penalty if full Year 1 fees not paid before arrival
- City University: 100 RM/month penalty for any outstanding balance
- UTM Space: additional 700 RM for official Offer Letter after receiving action letter
- NUMed: visa refund policy — EMGS fees are non-refundable, but 2,000 RM visa deposit can be reclaimed with written request if VAL not used
- Application fees range: Monash 106 RM → City University 1,000 RM

**Q: What scholarships are available at Malaysian universities?**
A: Notable scholarships:
- Nottingham Provost's Excellence: 100% tuition waiver (maintain 60% GPA every year)
- Nottingham Dean's Excellence: 25% discount for one academic year
- Nottingham Sports & Arts: up to 50% tuition discount
- Nottingham Sibling: 10% discount first year
- City University: 4,000 RM grant for Sudanese students (Year 1)

**Q: What are the airport arrival rules?**
A: Students must notify the university 3–7 days before arrival. Avoid arriving during Malaysian public holidays to prevent delays in airport clearance (Clearance) procedures. Elm w Noor provides airport reception service.

**Q: What photo requirements apply for Malaysian university/visa applications?**
A: Strict photo requirements:
- Pure white background with NO shadows on face or background
- Head perfectly centered, no tilting
- PROHIBITED: glasses (even prescription), jewelry, hair covering any part of face

**Q: What makes Malaysia good for Arab Muslim students?**
A: Malaysia is a Muslim-majority country ranked #13 globally in the Global Peace Index 2025 (in the "Very High Peace" category). Halal food is universally available (100%). Mosques are present everywhere. There is an Arab community of 200,000+ residents. Student cost of living: 400–700 USD/month for comfortable life (housing + food + transport).

**Q: What is the employment rate for Malaysian university graduates?**
A: UTeM: 97% employment rate, 30% receive job offers during their 6-month industrial training. UNITEN: 95% employment rate. UTM international student body: 5,468 out of 19,467 total students.
